Date: 2025-10-09
Time: 14:05 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Diego Morales, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Sara Lin, Matt O'Neal, Jamal Reyes (Blue Harbor Logistics)
Artifacts: shared spreadsheet (link), pilot-benchmarks.xlsx (link), runbook draft (link)
summary: Sprint 3 retrospective focused on continuous batching adjustments, observed tail latency during burst periods, and setting concurrency targets. Agreed on a small config change to increase concurrent workers to 16 and adjust batch max size to 28 with more aggressive KV-cache warmup. Next steps: Redwood to provide configs and micro-benchmarks; customer to run three traffic profiles and return results.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call...
[00:12] Sara: Sara here.
[00:15] Matt: Matt on infra.
[00:18] Jamal: Jamal ML.
[00:20] Diego: Diego from Redwood, I'll run through the bench and tuning notes.
[00:30] Avery: Cool, objective today is to review sprint 3 numbers and agree next steps for throughput.
[01:05] Diego: So we ran three windows, low, medium, high. Peak qps in the high window was about 950 requests per minute, average per-request tokens ~420, so tokens/sec equivalent was roughly 6.6k.
[01:35] Jamal: Those numbers match what we saw but the tail latency spike at 95th/99th was concerning, spiking to ~1.8s at 99th, is that from queue buildup?
[01:52] Diego: Yes, a mix - we hit continuous-batching thresholds that delayed first-token for some requests. Also KV cache misses during cold starts bumped kernel times.
[02:12] Matt: The worst window was the afternoon burst where concurrent sessions jumped from 10 to 26 in 30s. Autoscaling latencies compounded it.
[02:30] Avery: Right, so two levers: keep the concurrency target lower to avoid big queuing, or increase worker concurrency and micro-batch size to absorb bursts. There's cost tradeoff.
[02:48] Sara: Our success criteria is sub-700ms p95 and under 1s p99 for user-facing flows. Cost sensitivity is moderate.
[03:05] Diego: Proposed config change: set concurrency target to 16 (from 12), batch max size to 28, and reduce batch wait timeout from 20ms to 12ms to avoid long batching delays. Also pre-warm KV cache on session creation for known templates.
[03:30] Jamal: Pre-warm sounds promising but how do we force warmup without double tokens cost?
[03:45] Diego: We use a cheap prefix probe with short prompt to populate KV—very small token cost, can be done async. We'll include the script.
[04:03] Matt: Also we noticed queue size metric in the infra wasn't exported properly, some samples missing. We'll add more tagging.
[04:20] Priya: Noted. Diego, can you share the exact metric names so Blue Harbor can map them to their dashboards?
[04:30] Diego: Yes, sending list.
[05:00] Avery: Walkthrough of micro-benchmark results - Diego?
[05:10] Diego: Alright. In the baseline config p95 was 630ms, p99 1.3s. After we increased batch size to 24 in trial A p95 improved to ~580ms but p99 stayed high because queueing increased. Trial B bumped concurrency to 16 and batch max 28 - p95 ~570ms, p99 ~920ms under steady traffic but in burst traffic p99 moved to 1.1s.
[06:00] Jamal: So burst scenario still problematic. Could burst capacity fallback be useful? Like fallback to a smaller model for non-critical calls?
[06:12] Avery: Yes, we discussed automatic fallback to a lower-cost, lower-latency variant when queue > threshold. That’s supported. Need to define which paths are acceptable to degrade.
[06:30] Sara: For order-tracking flows we can tolerate summarized responses (smaller models). For billing we cannot.
[06:44] Matt: We need per-route rules.
[06:50] Diego: We'll add canary rules and a policy doc.
[07:10] Jamal: What's the KV cache hit-rate now? We saw like 68% during the trials?
[07:20] Diego: Correct overall ~68% during rolling windows, but for frequent templates it’s >90%. The long tail has many cold templates.
[07:35] Sara: Is there a way to pre-warm by user cohort?
[07:40] Diego: Yes, you can pin templates to a warm pool, or we can schedule small async probes on session init for high-value cohorts.
[08:00] Matt: On autoscaling - the cold spin-up time for Dedicated node allocation was around 45s in the worst case. That contributes to those mid-window spikes.
[08:18] Avery: For the pilot we recommended burst capacity be enabled with reserve nodes to reduce cold-start. That does increase monthly cost but smooths latency.
[08:32] Jamal: What about backpressure? Can Redwood reject or queue at API gateway level sooner to avoid deeper queue pileup?
[08:45] Diego: Yes we offer a token-bucket style gate at the ingress and soft-queue with abort thresholds; we can tune the gate to prioritize percent of requests. We'll provide suggested Ingress config.
[09:10] Sara: I want a clear SLA for retries and for user-visible timeouts.
[09:20] Priya: We'll draft recommended timeouts and retry logic for Blue Harbor flows.
[09:30] Diego: One more observation: continuous batching benefits when request inter-arrival is stable. In highly bursty traffic, aggressive batching harms p99. So we recommend adaptive batch sizing tied to concurrency signals.
[09:55] Jamal: Is adaptive batching in the roadmap?
[10:00] Diego: There's an experimental adaptive scheduler we can enable in pilot mode; it's not GA but we can run it behind a feature flag during the next window.
[10:15] Avery: Ok, decision points - do we enable adaptive batching and increase concurrency to 16 for the next test window?
[10:25] Sara: Yes to both, but add fallback to smaller model for non-critical routes.
[10:32] Matt: Agree. Also we'll patch the telemetry to capture queue size per route.
[10:40] Jamal: We'll provide sample traces from last week to help tune thresholds.
[10:50] Avery: We'll update configs and push them to the shared folder. Diego will post micro-bench scripts.
[11:05] Diego: Quick note - micro-benchmarks require a representative prompt set. Jamal please validate the prompt list in the sheet.
[11:18] Jamal: I'll validate by end of week.
[11:25] Sara: Who owns running the three windows? Blue Harbor or Redwood?
[11:30] Avery: Joint: Redwood will supply the bench runner and configs; Blue Harbor will execute inside their test env to ensure network topology parity.
[11:45] Priya: I'll coordinate scheduling.
[12:00] Matt: Regarding cost - can we get an estimate on delta if we increase concurrency and reserve 2 burst nodes?
[12:10] Avery: Yes, we'll include cost delta in the config spreadsheet.
[12:20] Jamal: Also add notes about expected token burn for KV pre-warm probing.
[12:28] Diego: Will do.
[12:35] Avery: Any blockers?
[12:40] Sara: Not yet, other than needing the configs and runbook.
[12:45] Matt: We need the extra metrics exported.
[12:48] Priya: We'll follow up on that.
[12:55] Avery: Ok recap - Redwood to share tuned configs + micro-bench script (Avery/Diego), Blue Harbor to run low/med/high windows and post results, then reconvene.
[13:12] Jamal: Sounds good.
[13:20] Sara: Thanks all.
[13:25] Avery: Meeting adjourned.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mislabels and ASR oddities; some technical terms may be spelled phonetically (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"), and product names abbreviated. Shared artifacts referenced only as links in the header.
